correctness.rationale: The two integer reflections give exactly the alternating prefix-counter updates by Pascal and reflected binomial identities, including j=1 and t<0. In F2[[X]], (1+X)^L=1+X^L gives the required periodicity through every j<L. The empty word gives zero in all positive coordinates; 01 advances one residue. Lucas's mask at u=k distinguishes the half-period shift and all smaller candidate periods divide that half-period. Every pair therefore has a common distinguishing suffix of the form (01)^a. An independent linear-algebra check: on the full prefix vector the two letter maps are involutions I+A,I+B, with A,B supported on complementary entries of the first subdiagonal. R=(I+B)(I+A)=I+U has U with unit first subdiagonal. U^j e0 first becomes nonzero at index j, and the order of R and orbit size of e0 are exactly L by characteristic-two squaring. The second involution fixes e0, so the whole orbit is the rotation orbit. For a difference with leading coordinate j, the kth coordinate of U^(k-j) times that difference is one; consequently some power of R distinguishes the pair. This also checks the lower bound independently of Lucas. Inspected the supporting files without executing uploaded programs; independently ran the fresh replay for 10,230 direct subset-count comparisons and exact orbit/output distinguishability at 14 dyadic boundary lengths through 128. The finite checks supplement, not replace, the all-length proof.
residual_risks: No claim for nonalternating words, other moduli, or models with different memory/output conventions.

value.rationale: A uniform, sharp streaming memory classification for a natural target family: 2^k candidate prefix patterns collapse to between k+1 and 2k actual states, with provably no further identifications. Two reflections and powers-of-two jumps explain why the natural periodic suffix is enough to distinguish states. This is considerably more than checking isolated examples or giving a general counter construction.
